title: Apixaban with a heparin lock flush for a port: not a duplicate

clinical_review.notes: Owner approved 2026-11-16 the four review points of changelog #187 as presented: the case and its reference answer, the reviewed reason, a 300 unit lock flush as not systemic, and naming the parenteral drug on a same-day start. The basis is the Eliquis label text quoted in #187 (2.5, 5.2, 7.3), read by Claude Code on DailyMed; the owner did not report reading the label.

story: A 68-year-old man with sigmoid colon cancer on chemotherapy through an implanted port, and on apixaban 5 mg twice daily for a left femoral vein thrombosis diagnosed in September, is admitted with dehydration after poor oral intake. Apixaban is continued. Nursing flushes the port with heparin 100 units/mL, 3 mL (300 units), after each access, per the port protocol. Weight 80 kg, creatinine 0.9 mg/dL.

problems.title: Acute thrombosis of left femoral vein

prescriptions.instructions: 5 mg by mouth twice daily (home medication continued)

prescriptions.drug: 3 ML heparin sodium, porcine 100 UNT/ML Prefilled Syringe
prescriptions.instructions: 300 units (3 mL) to flush the implanted port after each access, per protocol
4 mg by mouth every 8 hours as needed for nausea

results.text: Platelets [#/volume] in Blood by Automated count

reference_answer: No change. A heparin lock flush of 300 units keeps the port open and does not anticoagulate the patient; apixaban 5 mg twice daily continues for the femoral vein thrombosis.
rationale: A near miss for the duplicate anticoagulation rule: heparin is on the medication list, but as a lock flush, which the knowledge base does not count as a systemic anticoagulant. The rule must stay silent; treating every heparin product as anticoagulation would flood the queue with flush orders.

citations.supports: Concomitant heparin increases bleeding risk on apixaban (5.2, 7.3); switching stops one anticoagulant and starts the other at the next dose, without overlap (2.5). Content read in the label by Claude Code; owner approved 2026-11-16 (#189).
